From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@brightline-audit.com>

Subject: Question on period inclusivity / point-in-time snapshots for SOC 2 Type II

Hi David,

Thanks for sending the SOC 2 Type II report PDF earlier. Our external audit team at BrightLine is reviewing coverage boundaries and has a couple of technical questions before we close our findings for DataSigma. Please confirm the following so we can document it in the final memo:

1) The report lists the covered period as 2026-01-01 through 2026-12-31. For the purposes of evidence sampling, do you treat the period as inclusive of the entire calendar day on 2026-12-31 (i.e., up to 23:59:59 UTC), or do you apply a point-in-time cutoff (for example snapshots taken at 00:00 UTC on the next day)?

2) We observed a set of operational snapshots (log dumps) with timestamps recorded in PDT (America/Los_Angeles). If a snapshot file indicates events up to 2026-06-30 23:59:59 PDT, does Redwood consider those events within the June 2026 coverage month, given timezone normalization to UTC?

3) If Redwood uses a snapshot cutover that effectively excludes some events that occurred on the last calendar day (e.g., a snapshot taken at 00:00 on 2026-07-01), would BrightLine/our reviewing auditor expect a bridge letter to clarify partial-month inclusion/exclusion? The DataSigma compliance team has asked whether a short bridge letter would be sufficient to resolve this kind of boundary ambiguity.

Can you point us to any internal guidance you use for "day inclusivity" and whether you can produce a one-page bridge statement if needed? We may also request a sample of the log manifest showing timezone normalization for a small subset.

Appreciate a quick confirmation — our audit window is tight.

Best,
Alex Rivera
Senior Auditor
BrightLine Auditing

Subject: Re: Question on period inclusivity / point-in-time snapshots for SOC 2 Type II

Alex / Sandeep —

Thanks for the clear questions. Short answers up front, followed by the operational detail below.

Short answers:
- Our SOC 2 Type II coverage is intended to be inclusive through the final second of the listed last day (i.e., up to 23:59:59 UTC on 2026-12-31).
- We normalize all system timestamps internally to UTC for audit evidence. A snapshot that shows events up to 2026-06-30 23:59:59 PDT is treated as within June 2026 once converted to UTC.
- If an evidence snapshot was taken in a way that excluded events from the last calendar day (for example, a maintenance snapshot at 00:00 on 2026-07-01 that does not capture late-night events), we can provide a one-page bridge letter that explicitly states the snapshot cutover policy and which services are affected.

Operational detail (for the audit record):
1) Cutoff policy: our logging and archival pipeline converts all incoming timestamps to UTC at ingestion. For daily snapshot artifacts we define the inclusive range for a calendar date D as [D 00:00:00 UTC, D 23:59:59 UTC]. Snapshots generated for the next-day 00:00 UTC capture are treated as an archival capture of the closed period and should be considered inclusive of the prior day's events, provided the manifest indicates the latest event timestamp.

2) Timezone normalization: the CSV manifest we provide includes the original event timestamp, source timezone, and normalized_utc_timestamp columns. That manifest is what auditors rely on to reconcile local times with the UTC-based window.

3) Bridge letters: we maintain a short template bridge letter for partial-month edge cases that: (a) states the SOC 2 covered dates, (b) describes the snapshot generation cadence, (c) identifies services where telemetry is point-in-time versus continuous, and (d) lists any known limitations. We can adapt the template to call out inference runtime logs, KV-cache snapshots, and audit-log rollups if those are the focal items.

Attachments: I'm attaching the SOC 2 PDF you referenced and a proposed one-page bridge-letter draft (redlined). I'm also attaching a small log manifest sample showing timezone normalization for a June 30 sample.

Next steps: please confirm the exact scope DataSigma's auditor wants spelled out in the bridge letter (services + whether you require UTC-anchored examples). If agreeable, Marissa (GRC) and Tessa (Legal) will shepherd final language and sign-off. We can turn around a finalized bridge letter within 48 hours once we have the list.

-David

--

Thanks David — that helps. A couple of clarifications from the audit perspective:

- When you say "Snapshots generated for the next-day 00:00 UTC capture are treated as an archival capture of the closed period," can you confirm whether the manifest includes the maximum event timestamp, and whether you can certify (in the bridge letter) that no events with timestamps <= 2026-06-30 23:59:59 UTC were omitted from those archived snapshots? Our team prefers an explicit statement that the manifest's max_timestamp <= cutoff and that ingestion normalization is deterministic.

- For our scope, please include explicit mentions of: inference runtime request logs, system audit logs (who/what/when), and any KV-cache state snapshots you may use for replay testing. Calling out those items in the bridge letter will avoid follow-up evidence requests.

If you can provide the revised bridge letter language and an example manifest row for the June 30 snapshot, we can get back to you with a final auditor note — hopefully the same day.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Alex
